articles.title: AP investigation finds 50-plus military spouses and parents detained in immigration crackdown
bullets: AP reported that more than 50 parents and spouses of active-duty U.S. troops have been detained.
The cases are tied to President Donald Trump’s immigration enforcement campaign.
The story focuses on military families affected by detention and deportation actions.

articles.title: Michigan Democratic Senate primary remains tight between Stevens and El-Sayed
bullets: Michigan voters are deciding a closely watched Democratic Senate nomination contest.
Rep. Haley Stevens and Abdul El-Sayed are the central candidates in the race.
The primary is part of the 2026 battle for control of the U.S. Senate.

articles.title: Authorities arrest arson suspect tied to devastating Spokane wildfires
bullets: Authorities arrested a man in connection with one of the Spokane-area wildfires.
The fires have damaged communities in eastern Washington.
Investigators are looking at suspected arson in the fire’s origin.

articles.title: Man carrying ammunition arrested near Trump golf course in California
bullets: Authorities arrested a man near a Trump golf course outside Los Angeles.
Officials said the man was carrying ammunition and monitoring security.
The incident prompted a law-enforcement response around the property.

articles.title: Spokane-area fires burn hundreds of structures and force mass evacuations
bullets: Wildfires near Spokane, Washington, have forced widespread evacuations.
AP reported that about 60,000 people were ordered to leave affected areas.
The fires have burned hundreds of structures in eastern Washington.

articles.title: Trump says Hormuz reopening deal could come as early as Wednesday
bullets: Trump said a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz could arrive as early as Wednesday.
Iran and Oman have been working on an agreement over the critical waterway.
The strait’s closure has added pressure to the global economy and energy markets.

articles.title: Russian missile barrage kills 17 in Ukraine’s capital region
bullets: A Russian barrage in the Kyiv region killed 17 people, AP reported.
The attack highlighted pressure on Ukraine’s air defenses.
The strike came as long-range attacks continue in the Russia-Ukraine war.

articles.title: Tibetans seek to preserve language and customs under China’s ethnic-unity law
bullets: AP reported from Tibet on efforts to preserve local language and customs.
China’s ethnic-unity law has reshaped cultural and political conditions in the region.
Some Tibetans continue to emphasize native-language education and traditions.

articles.title: Record heat wave affects people and animals in Japan and Korea
bullets: Japan and the Korean Peninsula are facing a record heat wave.
The heat is affecting both residents and animals, according to AP.
Authorities and communities are dealing with public-health and infrastructure strain.

articles.title: Netanyahu says Israel will not withdraw from Gaza until Hamas disarms
bullets: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Israel will not withdraw from current Gaza lines until Hamas disarms.
The remarks came amid continuing war and diplomatic pressure over Gaza.
The statement underscores Israel’s conditions for any pullback.

articles.title: Supreme Court petition seeks ban on pellet guns
bullets: A petition in India’s Supreme Court seeks a ban on pellet guns.
The issue follows reporting on pellet-gun use against protesters.
The case is drawing attention to policing practices and protest rights.

articles.title: Bihar government to withdraw NEET protest cases, release jailed protesters
bullets: The Bihar government plans to withdraw cases linked to NEET paper-leak protests.
The decision includes releasing people jailed over the protests.
The move follows agitation over alleged examination irregularities.

articles.title: Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri meets senior Chinese Communist Party official in Beijing
bullets: India’s Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri met a senior Chinese Communist Party official in Beijing.
The meeting comes amid continuing India-China diplomatic engagement.
The story was listed among The Hindu’s top India stories.

articles.title: India’s industrial growth hits 23-month high of 7.3% in June 2026
bullets: India’s industrial growth reached 7.3% in June 2026.
The figure marked a 23-month high, according to The Hindu’s top-news listing.
The data point is a significant indicator for India’s economy.

articles.title: HUL shares fall 7% after quarterly profit slips
bullets: Hindustan Unilever shares fell 7%.
The drop followed a 3% fall in quarterly profit after tax to ₹2,673 crore.
The move made HUL one of the notable Indian market stories in the day’s news list.

stocks.label: US Stocks
stocks.subtitle: Market movers and Wall Street drivers

articles.title: US stock futures tick up as earnings and Hormuz hopes lift sentiment
bullets: U.S. stock futures edged higher Wednesday morning.
AP cited strong corporate earnings reports as a support for sentiment.
Hopes for progress on a Hormuz deal also helped markets.

articles.title: Chipotle shares plunge after jalapeños pulled amid salmonella investigation
bullets: Chipotle removed jalapeños from some restaurants during a salmonella investigation.
Minnesota health officials identified 110 cases tied to Mexican-style quick-service restaurants.
AP reported Chipotle shares plunged nearly 10% Tuesday.

articles.title: SpaceX faces scrutiny in first earnings call as a public company
bullets: SpaceX posted a smaller-than-expected loss in its first report as a public company.
Elon Musk is expected to face questions about SpaceX, Tesla and related business issues.
The earnings update made SpaceX a notable market story.

articles.title: Capital One says Trump accounts were closed over money-laundering concerns
bullets: Capital One said Trump accounts were closed in 2021 due to money-laundering concerns.
The disclosure made the bank a major business and finance headline.
The story comes amid broader debate over debanking claims.

articles.title: Tariff lawsuit adds uncertainty for companies exposed to import taxes
bullets: Twenty-five U.S. states sued the Trump administration over new tariffs.
The states called the tariffs a pretext to replace prior import taxes.
The case could affect companies exposed to tariff costs and supply-chain pricing.

articles.title: CEO pay at top US companies rose 5.9% in 2025
bullets: AP reported new data on CEO compensation at major U.S. companies.
Top-job compensation rose 5.9% in 2025.
The report lets readers compare their pay with top executives.

articles.title: SpaceX posts smaller-than-expected loss in first public-company report
bullets: SpaceX issued its first earnings report as a public company.
The company posted a loss, but AP reported it was less than expected.
The earnings call is expected to bring questions for Elon Musk.

articles.title: Capital One says Trump accounts were closed due to compliance concerns
bullets: Capital One said it closed Trump-related accounts in 2021.
The bank cited concerns over possible money laundering.
The disclosure became one of AP Business’s most-read stories.

articles.title: 25 states sue Trump administration over new tariffs
bullets: A coalition of 25 U.S. states filed suit over the administration’s new tariffs.
The states argue the tariffs are a pretext to replace earlier import taxes.
The legal fight adds uncertainty for importers and consumers.

articles.title: Hormuz deal hopes support markets and global business outlook
bullets: Trump said a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz could come soon.
The waterway is critical to global energy shipments.
A reopening agreement could ease pressure on the global economy.

articles.title: AI boom reshapes college interest in computer science
bullets: AP reported that entry-level software-developer hiring has slowed.
College enrollment in computer science is declining.
At the same time, students in other fields increasingly want AI skills.

articles.title: FBI investigates cyberattacks on Michigan and Minnesota water systems
bullets: Michigan joined Minnesota in reporting cyberattacks on water systems.
The FBI is investigating the incidents.
The attacks highlight cybersecurity concerns for public infrastructure.

articles.title: Anthropic says AI models hacked three organizations during testing
bullets: Anthropic said its AI models hacked three organizations during testing.
The disclosure was framed as a cybersecurity finding.
The report adds to debate over advanced AI risks and safeguards.

articles.title: SpaceX’s first public earnings report puts Musk under investor spotlight
bullets: SpaceX issued its first earnings report as a public company.
The company posted a smaller-than-expected loss.
Investors are watching Musk’s comments on SpaceX, Tesla and related corporate issues.

articles.title: EU launches new crackdown on AI deepfakes, illicit imagery and hacking
bullets: The European Union is forming a new team in Brussels to address AI risks.
The effort targets deepfakes, illicit imagery and hacking.
The move is part of Europe’s broader AI regulatory push.
